notes: QBTS 10-K narrative is light on named Pentagon programs / PE numbers. The company frames itself as a commercial quantum vendor with a thin federal-customer overlay (CDAO Tradewinds 'awardable' status, a system hosted at Davidson Technologies in Huntsville, AL, and a missile-defense PoC with Anduril). Customer A = 67% of FY2025 revenue is the single most material concentration disclosure; the company does NOT name Customer A but other text strongly implies Forschungszentrum Juelich (FZJ) — a German national-research lab, NOT a DoD program. Few claims fit the canonical 'named Pentagon PE' pattern. We extract DoD-adjacent claims, customer-concentration claims, the Quantum Circuits acquisition pivot, and two control (non-J-Book) claims.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave achieved 'awardable' status through the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office's (CDAO) Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace, positioning the company to capture U.S. government revenue.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: ...achievement of awardable status through the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office's Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace, D-Wave has increased its capabilities in support of United States government customers...

claims.claim_text: Davidson Technologies hosts the second U.S.-based D-Wave Advantage2 quantum computer in Huntsville, AL, to 'eventually run sensitive applications' in support of U.S. government and aerospace customers.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: Davidson Technologies hosts the second U.S.-based D-Wave Advantage2 quantum computer at its global headquarters in Huntsville, Alabama. The system will eventually run sensitive applications using quantum computing technology.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave worked with Davidson Technologies and Anduril Industries on an initial proof-of-concept for complex missile-defense planning scenarios, showing >=10x speedup and ability to intercept an additional 45-60 missiles in a 500-missile attack simulation.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: Most recently, we worked with Davidson Technologies and Anduril Industries Inc., a defense technology company focused on advanced autonomous systems, to develop an initial proof-of-concept for complex missile-defense planning scenarios. Compared to classical solvers, D-Wave's Stride hybrid solver delivered at least 10x faster time-to-solution, a 9% to 12% improvement in threat mitigation, and the ability to intercept an additional 45-60 missiles in a 500-missile attack simulation.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave has formed a new business unit dedicated to driving adoption of quantum computing products and services with the U.S. government, led by a 'seasoned public sector business executive'.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: ...the formation of a new business unit dedicated to driving the adoption of quantum computing products and services with the U.S. government, led by a seasoned public sector business executive.

claims.claim_text: One customer ('Customer A') represented 67% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 (up from 17% in 2024); customer is not named.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.object_value: 67% of FY2025 revenue from a single undisclosed customer
claims.source_quote: Year Ended December 31, 2025 2024 Customer A 67 % 17 % As of each of December 31, 2025 and 2024, there were five and three significant customers, respectively, that comprised ten percent or more of outstanding accounts receivable balances.

claims.claim_text: Forschungszentrum Juelich (FZJ) purchased the D-Wave Advantage quantum computer in February 2025 — the first HPC center in the world to own a D-Wave annealing system — and upgraded to Advantage2 during 2025.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: in February 2025, D-Wave announced that FZJ has purchased this quantum computer, becoming the first high-performance computing center in the world to own a D-Wave Advantage annealing quantum computing system. This system was upgraded to an Advantage2 quantum computer throughout 2025.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave closed acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc. on January 20, 2026 — a developer of error-corrected superconducting gate-model quantum computing systems — as the centerpiece of a pivot to dual-platform (annealing + gate-model) thesis.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: On January 20, 2026, D-Wave announced the completion of its acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc., a leading developer of error-corrected superconducting gate-model quantum computing systems. With this acquisition, we believe that D-Wave has solidified its position as the world's first and only dual-platform quantum computing company...

kwargs.parent_thesis: Commercial annealing quantum computing systems delivered via cloud (Leap service) for enterprise optimization use cases; expanding to gate-model.

acquisitions.target_business: Error-corrected superconducting dual-rail gate-model quantum computers (Yale spinout)

claims.claim_text: D-Wave will make an 'initial gate-model quantum computer generally available in 2026' — a forward technology milestone for a product line acquired only 4 months earlier.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: We have commercialized annealing quantum computers, and plan to make an initial gate-model quantum computer generally available in 2026.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave has identified 'unique research and government classified applications that require secure cloud or stand-alone systems (potentially for both annealing and gate-model systems) on customer premises' as a growth vector.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: Secure computing: We anticipate that there may be unique research and government classified applications that require secure cloud or stand-alone systems (potentially for both annealing and gate-model systems) on customer premises.

claims.claim_text: D-Wave Government Inc. is the primary federal contracting entity for D-Wave Quantum Inc. (per Exhibit 21).
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: [Exhibit 21] D-Wave Government Inc. — federal contracting entity (per ticker_entity_resolution.json).

claims.claim_text: Control claim: D-Wave has installed quantum systems at Forschungszentrum Juelich, USC Information Sciences Institute, and Davidson Technologies — three distinct geographic locations.
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.object_value: Burnaby BC; USC ISI (Marina del Rey); FZJ (Germany); Davidson Technologies (Huntsville AL)
claims.source_quote: ...different geographical locations, including at our Quantum Center of Excellence in Burnaby, British Columbia, at the University of Southern California's Information Sciences Institute (ISI) and at Davidson Technologies in Huntsville, Alabama.

claims.claim_text: Control claim: D-Wave generated $24.6M total revenue in FY2025 vs $8.8M in FY2024 (179% YoY growth).
claims.subject: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
claims.source_quote: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we generated revenue totaling $24.6 million and $8.8 million, respectively.
